description: A long first-row gap means the entire interval between successive row leaders is already covered by the current product frontier P_n = R_n C_n. This card proposes importing covering-system style interval certificates to show that such full coverage forces a rigid witness pattern that may be uniformly bounded.
mathematical_formalization: Let R_n={r_1,...,r_n}, C_n={c_1,...,c_n}, P_n={r_i c_j : i,j\le n}. If g_n=r_{n+1}-r_n, then [r_n+1, r_n+g_n-1] \subseteq P_n. Seek L such that any interval I of length > L cannot admit witness sets W(x)={(r,c)\in R_n\times C_n: rc=x} for every x\in I without violating an uncovered-set density bound.
analogical_connections: covering-system certificates for impossible dense covers
hypergraph shadow witnesses for consecutive constraints
proof certificates for SAT instances with highly correlated clauses
implementation_hypothesis: At each record gap, extract one minimal divisor witness per covered integer, compress the interval into a set-cover instance, and test whether the witness family necessarily induces a forbidden overlap pattern. A successful certificate search would produce a finite catalog of local obstructions whose nonappearance bounds g_n.
experiment_seed: Compute record gaps up to at least n=10^4, extract minimal witness families for each interior integer in those intervals, and cluster the certificates by overlap graph. A stable finite motif library would be strong evidence for a bounded-gap proof path.

novelty_claim: The new step is to treat consecutive covered integers in T as an endogenous covering system whose moduli and residues come from divisor witnesses, rather than from an externally prescribed congruence family.
differentiation: This is not a reimplementation of covering-systems work because the certificate objects are generated by the mex frontier and must explain a dynamic multiplication table, not a fixed family of residue classes.

description: Ford-style divisor-window asymptotics give a natural control model for how densely a sparse product set can fill short intervals. The idea is to compare the mex-generated frontier to an exogenous multiplication table with the same divisor-profile statistics and use that as a benchmark for gap growth.
mathematical_formalization: For x near r_n, define H_n(x)=\sum_{d\mid x} 1_{d\in R_n}1_{x/d\in C_n}. Then x\in P_n iff H_n(x)\ge 1. Approximate \mathbb{P}[H_n(x)=0] via divisor-window densities for d in [x/y, x/z], and bound \max\{h:[x,x+h]\cap P_n=\emptyset\} using local estimates for H_n.
implementation_hypothesis: Estimate H_n(x) empirically on sliding windows, smooth by divisor-profile buckets, and compare the resulting gap tail to Ford-type asymptotics. If the empirical tail is much lighter than the control law, the mex feedback is creating extra regularity worth proving.
experiment_seed: For n up to 6000, regress observed uncovered-block lengths against empirical divisor-window intensity and compare with a null model built from shuffled R_n and C_n of the same size.

description: Modular Stanley sequences show that greedy rules can hide large-gap mechanisms behind arithmetic congruence structure. This card asks whether the T frontier admits a multiplicative analog: residue or ratio obstructions that repeatedly force long covered blocks before the next row leader appears.
mathematical_formalization: Search for q and residue sets A_q,B_q such that R_n \bmod q \subseteq A_q, C_n \bmod q \subseteq B_q, and the product set A_q B_q leaves a structured family of residue classes over- or under-covered. A disproof route would construct q_k with interval-supporting obstructions; a proof route would rule out persistent q-stable holes.
analogical_connections: forbidden pattern cascades in cellular automata
implementation_hypothesis: Build residue heatmaps for q up to a few hundred at record-gap times, then mine for persistent holes or unusually dense classes. If no stable obstruction survives scale changes, that weakens the main route to unbounded gaps.
experiment_seed: At each record gap, store occupancy vectors for R_n and C_n modulo q<=200 and run change-point tests on the most deviant moduli.

description: The raw gap sequence may hide a much lower-complexity symbolic process if gaps are encoded by the divisor-witness type that explains them. This card proposes learning a substitution or morphic law on those witness symbols rather than on the numeric gaps themselves.
mathematical_formalization: Choose a finite signature map \sigma_n = \Sigma(\text{local witness pattern around } r_n). Seek a morphism \varphi: \mathcal{A}\to \mathcal{A}^* and coding \tau such that \sigma = \tau(\varphi^\omega(a_0)) and d_n = f(\sigma_n) for a low-complexity observable f.
implementation_hypothesis: Build a symbolic alphabet from local factorization certificates near each row gap, then run substitution mining, suffix automata, and compression tests. If a low-entropy symbolic code exists, it should compress record-gap neighborhoods far better than gap values alone.
experiment_seed: Train a symbolic encoder on the first 4000 row gaps, fit candidate substitutions, and test predictive cross-entropy on the next 2000 gaps against iid and Markov baselines.

description: A coarser explanation may exist even if T is not exactly automatic: the row and column leaders could shadow complementary Beatty pairs with bounded local noise. mathematical_formalization: Fit r_n = \lfloor \alpha n + u_n \rfloor and c_n = \lfloor \beta n + v_n \rfloor with \alpha \approx \beta and sublinear or bounded-block errors u_n,v_n. Test whether d_n \in D for a small set D and whether u_n,v_n correlate with Ostrowski/Fibonacci numeration classes.
analogical_connections: quantization noise around a linear drift
implementation_hypothesis: Estimate coarse slopes on growing windows, then stratify deviations by Ostrowski digits and Beatty residue classes. If deviations organize around numeration structure, Beatty machinery becomes a plausible proof scaffold.
experiment_seed: Fit alpha and beta from n<=6000, compute deviation histograms on multiple scales, and test whether record-gap times cluster in specific numeration classes.

description: Automatic-sequence theory can also be used negatively: any automatic model that directly encodes prime-side membership is likely too rigid. This card turns classification theorems for multiplicative automatic sequences into a falsifier for overly simplistic conjectures about T.
mathematical_formalization: Define a candidate sign map \chi(p)\in\{\pm1\} by whether prime p first appears on row 1 or column 1, and extend completely multiplicatively. If \chi were k-automatic, classification results force eventual character-like rigidity incompatible with observed composite leader placement; therefore any finite-state model must act on frontier states, not on \chi alone.

implementation_hypothesis: Encode candidate low-state automata for prime-side labels, propagate them to composites, and search for contradictions against observed row/column leaders. Small-state infeasibility certificates prune the conjecture space before positive model building.
experiment_seed: Run a SAT/SMT search over k-automatic sign models with a small state budget using the first few hundred assigned primes and border composites as constraints.

description: The product frontier induces a highly heterogeneous divisor-incidence network: integers are covered when some left-right divisor pair activates them. This card studies record gaps as a percolation or matching phenomenon on that arithmetic graph rather than as a raw sequence problem.
mathematical_formalization: For each x \le X define E_x = \{(r,c)\in R_n\times C_n : rc=x\}. Coverage of x means E_x\neq\emptyset. Aggregate the E_x into a bipartite divisor graph with degree distribution inherited from divisor counts and analyze consecutive covered blocks via branching or matching heuristics.
analogical_connections: online bipartite matching with forbidden edges
implementation_hypothesis: Construct local divisor-incidence graphs around record gaps and compare them with degree-preserving random bipartite surrogates. If T consistently lives in a supercritical coverage regime while null models do not, the arithmetic structure is doing real work.
experiment_seed: For each record gap interval, compute degree statistics of the covering witness graph and compare against shuffled and configuration-model baselines.

description: Uncovered integers near the frontier can be treated phenomenologically as vacancies in a one-dimensional exclusion process. The mex rule always repairs the leftmost vacancy, so bounded differences would correspond to a jammed regime with uniformly short vacancy clusters.
mathematical_formalization: Let H_n(x)=1[x\notin P_n]. Study the run-length distribution of H_n on [1, r_n+W] for moving windows W and compare its cluster statistics to parking/RSA observables such as mean gap, skewness, kurtosis, and nearest-gap correlations.
implementation_hypothesis: Measure uncovered-cluster statistics and test whether they stabilize after rescaling by the frontier. A close match to jammed-process statistics would justify importing jamming heuristics as a phenomenological guide, even if not as a proof.
experiment_seed: Track uncovered-run histograms and higher moments across logarithmically spaced n, then compare with Page-Rényi and RSA reference values.

description: A fluid-limit approximation may separate average behavior from rare obstruction events. This card compresses the arithmetic state into divisor-profile buckets and fits a Wormald-style drift model that predicts how average gap and record-gap scales should evolve.

implementation_hypothesis: Use computed trajectories to fit bucket-level drifts and forecast future gap records. If the fitted model predicts bounded or slowly varying local gaps despite unbounded record times, it clarifies what sort of proof obstruction remains.
experiment_seed: Fit drift models on the first 2000 steps, forecast the next 4000, and compare predicted record-gap counts against the exact simulation.

description: The border sequences are chosen by two consecutive mex operations before the multiplicative interior is updated, so there is a natural complementary-sequence skeleton underneath the full process. This card isolates that skeleton and treats the interior products as a perturbative correction term.
mathematical_formalization: Let m_n(1)<m_n(2)<\cdots be the missing values of P_n. Then (r_{n+1}, c_{n+1})=(m_n(1), m_n(2)). Seek coarse recurrences r_{n+1}=F(r_{\le n},c_{\le n})+\Delta^R_n and c_{n+1}=G(r_{\le n},c_{\le n})+\Delta^C_n where F,G are complementary-sequence laws and \Delta captures multiplicative corrections.
analogical_connections: twin queues sharing a service discipline
implementation_hypothesis: Fit the best low-memory complementary model to the observed border sequences, then study the correction terms for bounded memory, numeration structure, or rare spikes. If corrections are local enough, bounded row gaps may follow from a finite-state perturbation theorem.
experiment_seed: Infer low-order state machines for (r_n,c_n) and their correction terms on n<=3000, then evaluate predictive stability on the next 3000 steps.
